blocks.text: The IoT Growth in the Near Future & the MVNO Opportunity

The IoT market is growing fast—it will be worth nearly $2.95 trillion in 2024 and is expected to cross $17 trillion by 2037 7, according to research firm Nester . Every day, millions of smart devices connect across industries like manufacturing, healthcare, logistics, and smart cities.
This surge is driven by 5G, AI, edge computing, and rapid tech innovation. While traditional Mobile Network Operators (MNOs) have powered IoT connectivity, MVNOs are now stepping in.

Mobile Virtual Network Operators (MVNOs) are cost-effective, flexible, and built to scale—exactly what IoT may need. With the MVNO market set to hit $14 billion by 2032, this space offers a major growth opportunity.
In this article, we’ll examine how MVNOs can capitalize on the IoT boom and lead the next wave of connected innovation.
What will you gain from this article?

A clear understanding of why IoT is a major growth opportunity for MVNOs in 2025 and beyond. Insights into the key connectivity technologies power IoT, from NB-IoT to 5G and eSIM. Real-world examples of how MVNOs successfully launch and scale in the IoT space. A breakdown of the industries where MVNOs can offer high-value, niche IoT solutions. Practical guidance on how Spenza helps MVNOs build, manage, and grow their IoT businesses.
Understanding the IoT Connectivity Spectrum for MVNOs

MVNOs lease network capacity from traditional telecom providers (MNOs) and resell it with their own pricing, services, and specializations. To fully understand how MVNOs enable IoT connectivity , it helps to look at the different types of connectivity they can offer.

blocks.text: How IoT Connectivity Can Help MVNOs Grow?
The world of connected devices is expanding fast, and MVNOs are in the perfect spot to grow. Here’s how getting into IoT can help them scale and stand out.
1. Smarter Pricing, Lower Costs

Most IoT devices use very little data, but companies usually connect thousands. This gives MVNOs a chance to buy data in bulk at better rates. They can then pass on the savings by offering flexible plans like pay-as-you-go or shared bundles. Customers get more value, and MVNOs stay competitive.
2. Simpler Network Management

With so many devices out there, managing connectivity can get tricky. MVNOs can use smart tools to handle everything in one place—from tracking SIMs/eSIMs and switching networks to solving issues quickly. That means fewer outages and better service for their customers.
3. Going Beyond Just Data

MVNOs don’t have to stop selling data. They can add services like device tracking, usage reports, or security updates. These extras help customers get more out of their devices—and give MVNOs a real edge over competitors offering basic plans.
4. Reaching Hard-to-Connect Areas

Not every device is in a city. Some are on farms, in remote towns, or out at sea. MVNOs can serve these places by mixing cellular coverage with other options like satellite or long-range radio. This helps them support industries like agriculture, logistics, and maritime—where others can’t reach.
5. New Ways to Make Money

MVNOs can build lasting customer relationships by selling data and offering setup support, tech help, or insights into device usage. These services turn one-time users into long-term customers and add new revenue streams.
Key Strategies for MVNOs to Capitalize on IoT in 2025

Now that you know how IoT connectivity can help MVNO, you know IoT is a real business opportunity for MVNOs. But tapping into this growing market takes more than offering SIM cards. MVNOs need a clear game plan that helps them stand out, offer real value, and build long-term success.
Here’s a simple, step-by-step blueprint for how MVNOs can successfully break into and grow in the IoT space.
1. Start by Finding the Right Niche

Not all IoT use cases are the same. Each industry has different needs, from the type of devices used to how much data is required. Instead of trying to serve everyone, MVNOs should pick specific verticals where they can offer focused value.
Some high-potential sectors include:

Smart Cities: Connect lighting systems, traffic control, parking sensors, and public safety devices. Industrial IoT: Support sensors in factories, supply chains, and machinery for real-time monitoring and automation. Healthcare: Enable remote monitoring devices, wearable trackers, and connected hospital tools. Logistics & Fleet: Track vehicle locations, temperatures, and delivery performance across borders. Agriculture: Connect soil sensors, irrigation systems, and livestock monitors in rural areas.
The key is to research pain points in these industries and offer solutions that fit their unique needs.
2. Build a Complete IoT Package
Selling data alone won’t cut it. Businesses today are looking for end-to-end solutions, tools that can manage their devices and data easily.
MVNOs can create ready-to-use packages that include:

Connectivity: Tailored data plans that match the usage patterns of IoT devices (e.g., low-data sensors vs. high-data video devices). Device Management: Dashboards to monitor, activate, or deactivate devices remotely. Security: Tools to protect customer data, ensure privacy, and prevent cyber threats. Analytics: Real-time insights that help customers track usage, detect issues early, or improve efficiency.
Offering these bundled services can turn MVNOs into trusted partners.
3. Partner to Build a Strong Ecosystem
MVNOs don’t have to do everything alone. Partnering with the right players can speed up time to market, lower costs, and expand capabilities.
Here’s who to team up with:

Device Manufacturers: Work with IoT hardware makers to offer pre-connected devices. Software Providers: Integrate with platforms that handle analytics, dashboards, or device data. System Integrators: These are the companies that bring together hardware, software, and services for the end customer that are essential for bigger projects. Connectivity Platforms: Partner with platforms like Spenza, which help with SIM/eSIM provisioning, cost tracking, and billing automation.
Together, this ecosystem allows MVNOs to launch faster, scale better, and support more use cases across industries.
4. Choose the Right Business Model
Once you’ve defined the niche and offering, it’s time to think about how you’ll price and sell it. The right model makes your business sustainable while giving customers flexibility.
Here are a few options:

Pay-as-You-Go: Great for startups or businesses with fluctuating usage pay only for what they use. Tiered Subscriptions: Offer packages by usage (e.g., 100MB/month, 500MB/month) or number of devices. Revenue Sharing: In some partnerships, you can co-brand services and split the earnings with hardware or software partners. White-Label Reselling: Let businesses rebrand and resell your IoT service as their own.
Your pricing strategy should reflect both customer value and operational cost. Keep it simple, clear, and scalable. Refer to this ” How mvnos make money ” article to understand this topic in detail.
MVNOs already have a head start in flexibility and affordability, by following key steps mentioned above, they can turn the IoT wave into long-term growth.
Challenges in the IoT MVNO Space
While IoT offers big opportunities, it’s not all smooth sailing. MVNOs entering this space need to be ready for a few bumps along the way.
1. Managing Lots of Devices at Scale

IoT setups can start with a few sensors and grow into tens of thousands across multiple countries. These devices come in all types, and keeping them connected smoothly is no small job. Without a solid system to manage everything in real time, things can spiral out of control.
2. Keeping Data Safe and Private

Security is a big deal. Customers want to know their data is protected, especially with strict privacy rules across different regions. MVNOs need the right tools like encryption and real-time threat monitoring—to secure things and build trust.
3. Reliable Service Is a Must

Some IoT use cases such as hospital equipment or factory machines can’t afford downtime. The connection has to work, no matter what. MVNOs need reliable tools to spot problems early, reroute traffic, and keep things running without hiccups.
4. Standing Out in a Busy Market

With more MVNOs entering the IoT space, the market is getting crowded. Simply offering cheap data isn’t enough. To win, MVNOs must deliver real value, like custom plans, industry-specific tools, and hands-on support that bigger providers often overlook.
Building these capabilities from scratch takes time, money, and deep expertise, and not every MVNO has that luxury. That’s where Spenza comes in.

Spenza is designed to make life easier for MVNOs. We give you everything you need: connectivity tools, billing and cost tracking, SIM and eSIM management, real-time analytics, and ready-to-use apps. With Spenza, MVNOs can focus on what matters most: launching faster, scaling smarter, and staying ahead of the curve.
How does Spenza Empower MVNOs in the IoT Space?

Spenza is built from the ground up to help MVNOs thrive in the fast-moving world of IoT. With its operator-neutral platform, Spenza simplifies IoT connectivity and makes it easy for businesses to launch, manage, and grow their own branded mobile services without the overhead of running a full telecom network.

Case Study: Spenza helped Butlr Scale to Deploy Smart IoT Devices

Butlr is a growing technology company that builds smart, privacy-focused thermal sensors. Their main product, Heatic 2+, helps businesses track occupancy and movement in offices, retail stores, senior living spaces, and smart buildings without using cameras. It’s a simple, effective way to gain people’s insights while respecting privacy.

As Butlr expanded into global markets like the U.S., U.K., and France, staying connected across borders became challenging. Managing different data plans, providers, and telecom costs in each country took time and created unnecessary complexity. And with real-time data flowing from thousands of devices, unlimited plans weren’t always cost-effective.

Spenza gave Butlr a single platform to manage all their mobile connectivity needs. With one dashboard, they could see where their data was going, track usage across countries, and switch to plans that better fit their actual needs.
What Changed with Spenza

Lower Costs: By ditching unlimited plans that weren’t fully used, Butlr cut down on telecom expenses. Simplified Management: No more juggling between different carriers and spreadsheets—Spenza brought it all into one place. Better Insights: Real-time reports helped the team make smarter choices about plans and usage. Scalable Setup: As Butlr rolls out new devices and enters new markets, its connectivity setup is ready to grow.

Now, Butlr spends less time dealing with telecom logistics and more time focusing on what they do best—building smart, privacy-first tech for the future of connected spaces. Spenza made it easy for them to stay in control, even as their operations scaled globally.
The Future of IoT for MVNOs: Trends to Watch Beyond 2025

As we look beyond 2025, the IoT landscape is expanding fast, and MVNOs are in a strong position to lead. With billions of devices coming online, businesses need flexible, secure, and scalable connectivity. Here’s how MVNOs can stay ahead in this evolving space.
Surge in Connected Devices

IoT connections are expected to exceed 75 billion devices globally. Industries like logistics, healthcare, and smart cities are driving this surge. MVNOs can serve these markets with affordable, scalable connectivity that adapts as deployments grow.
eSIM Becomes the New Standard

eSIMs simplify global connectivity by eliminating the need for physical SIM cards. MVNOs that support remote provisioning and multi-carrier switching will offer a major advantage to IoT businesses that operate across borders.
Rise of IoT-Focused MVNOs

New MVNOs are emerging with one goal—serving IoT use cases. These providers offer custom plans for smart devices in sectors like agriculture, fleet tracking, and industrial automation. Their niche focus enables faster deployment and more value-added services.
Security Takes Center Stage

With more devices online, protecting data and preventing breaches is a top concern. MVNOs must offer secure onboarding, encrypted communication, and real-time threat detection. Platforms like Spenza already provide this level of built-in security and compliance.
Sustainability Drives Smarter Connectivity

Energy-efficient devices and smarter network usage are becoming priorities. MVNOs that offer low-power connectivity and help optimize resource consumption will meet the rising demand for greener tech. Tools like Spenza help monitor usage and reduce overhead to support sustainable growth.
MVNOs that keep pace with these trends, with their in-office operations or with the help of platforms like Spenza, will become key players in powering the future of connected devices.
Conclusion

The IoT market in 2025 is bigger and more promising than ever. With billions of connected devices, rising demand across industries, and the growing need for flexible, global connectivity—MVNOs are perfectly positioned to take the lead.

The opportunities are massive, from eSIM technology and edge-powered networks to specialized, niche IoT services. But success won’t come from waiting. Now is the time for MVNOs to move strategically, build smarter offerings, focus on real customer needs, and scale confidently.
Spenza is here to help you do just that. Whether you’re starting fresh or looking to grow your IoT MVNO business, Spenza gives you the tools to launch, manage, and scale, all from a single platform.

MVNOs can provide NB-IoT, LTE-M, LoRaWAN, and 5G—each suited to different device needs, such as low data use, mobility, long range, or ultra-fast speed.

blocks.text: Introduction

eSIM technology is transforming how Mobile Virtual Network Operators (MVNOs) deploy and manage IoT connectivity. Unlike traditional SIM cards, eSIMs enable remote provisioning, multi-network flexibility, and centralized lifecycle management without requiring physical SIM replacement. This allows MVNOs to deploy connected devices faster, reduce operational costs, and scale global IoT services more efficiently.

By 2026, more than 2 billion eSIM-capable smartphones are in active use globally, while eSIM adoption continues to expand rapidly across wearables, laptops, connected vehicles, and enterprise IoT devices.

As enterprise IoT deployments continue to grow, eSIM has become a foundational technology for managing distributed device fleets across multiple carriers and regions. It simplifies onboarding, improves operational agility, strengthens security, and supports flexible business models for connected devices.

This guide explains how eSIM reshapes IoT services for MVNOs, the operational challenges it solves, implementation best practices, and how modern connectivity platforms simplify large-scale eSIM deployments..
What Is an MVNO eSIM?

An MVNO eSIM is an embedded programmable SIM that enables Mobile Virtual Network Operators (MVNOs) to remotely provision, activate, and manage mobile network profiles without requiring physical SIM cards. It simplifies IoT deployments by supporting remote connectivity management, multi-network flexibility, and centralized lifecycle operations across large fleets of connected devices.
eSIM’s Role in Transforming IoT MVNO Connectivity

eSIMs are shaking up the IoT MVNO connectivity space by directly confronting the limitations of traditional SIM cards. Remote provisioning allows deployment without all the headaches of dealing with physical SIM for big projects. With improved flexibility, MVNO eSIM devices can switch between networks without interruption and can stay connected across different contexts. Due to fast and seamless network expansion, eSIMs should facilitate connected device deployment, which is vital for large-scale IoT realization. Embedded technology enhances the security fabric against unauthorized access. eSIMs set higher levels of security, which are critical against unauthorized access.

Global cellular IoT connections reached approximately 4.5 billion by the end of 2025 and are projected to continue growing rapidly as enterprises deploy more connected devices across logistics, healthcare, manufacturing, and smart infrastructure.
Overcoming IoT Challenges with eSIMs for MVNOs

Managing numerous IoT devices requires a complex setup, which poses difficulties for MVNO eSIM deployments. Traditional SIM cards create logistical challenges and present scaling limitations and security vulnerabilities. eSIM technology provides an advanced solution that enhances connectivity while enabling MVNOs to address its challenges.
1. Pain Point: Roaming Restrictions & Costs

Many IoT deployments require operating devices across different regions, often leading to costly and unreliable roaming agreements. Permanent roaming restrictions can lead to unexpectedly disconnected devices, disrupting mission-critical operations. Though MVNOs provide multi-network access, they frequently fall back on roaming, which creates performance problems.

eSIM Solution: eSIMs eliminate traditional roaming through direct device connection to local networks. The solution eliminates costly performance and roaming problems and provides constant connectivity across locations. Through this solution, MVNOs bring seamless global coverage to their customers while avoiding complex multiple roaming agreements.
2. Pain Point: Logistical Nightmares

Managing physical SIM cards for thousands of IoT devices presents extreme logistical challenges. The process requires substantial time and budget to purchase the cards, deliver them, activate them, and manage potential replacements. For MVNOs, this translates to high operational costs and a delayed time to market for new IoT solutions.

eSIM Solution: eSIMs enable simple device administration through remote provisioning and activation functions. Network connection and update capabilities eliminate physical SIM card handling requirements. eSIMs bring significant operational cost reductions and simplify MVNOs’ deployment processes.
3. Pain Point: Scalability Bottlenecks

Traditional SIM cards become problematic when attempting large-scale IoT system deployments. Adding new devices demands purchasing and deploying physical SIM cards, which becomes complicated on a big scale. This challenge restricts IoT MVNOs from expanding customer numbers and developing new services.

eSIM Solution: eSIMs provide IoT networks with easy scaling capabilities. Remote provisioning enables new device additions without physical SIM cards and associated logistical challenges. MVNO eSIMs can expand their operations at speed through this solution to match IoT market growth.
4. Pain Point: Security Weaknesses

Traditional SIM cards are vulnerable to these kinds of attacks since they can be physically accessed and stolen. As IoT devices send sensitive data, it’s essential to protect that data during transmission, and physical SIM cards can be a weak point in the chain of security.

eSIM Solution: eSIM has better security features. They are less vulnerable to tampering or removal from storage and thus less likely to be compromised. eSIMs offer a layer of security beyond themselves and are here to stay as they are essential to safeguarding MVNO’s IoT implementations.
How Should eSIM Integration for MVNOs Happen?
This step-by-step approach helps with eSIM integration for MVNOs to implement eSIM technology.
Phase 1: Strategic Planning

Start with a clear vision. Analyze your target market (consumers, businesses, IoT) and their connectivity requirements. Assess how eSIMs can satisfy market demands while creating distinct value propositions. Choose partners equipped with strong SM-DP+ solutions together with eSIM expertise. Establish adaptable pricing models that support either usage-based billing or subscription-based strategies. Comply with all applicable telecommunications regulations, particularly those regarding data privacy.
Phase 2: Provisioning Framework

Build a solid provisioning framework. The SM-DP+ platform plays an essential role in managing eSIM profiles securely, so understanding its function is vital for eSIM profile delivery. Make sure to achieve smooth integration between your system and the SM-DP+. Use test kits and eSIMs to test the provisioning process thoroughly. Create subscription models that provide flexibility to serve different customer segments. Implement automation for self-service activation via QR codes or apps for a frictionless customer experience.
Phase 3: System Integration & Scaling

Secure connections via reliable APIs enable billing systems, CRMs, and network management systems to integrate with eSIM solutions. eSIM platform data must synchronize real time with your core systems for accurate billing records and customer information. Design user-friendly onboarding and self-service interfaces to support eSIM Integration for MVNOs and provide a smooth user experience

Global 5G subscriptions are expected to approach 3 billion by the end of 2026, accelerating demand for remote eSIM provisioning and scalable connectivity management across enterprise IoT deployments. The solution must be scalable to adapt to future growth alongside new technology implementations.
Phase 4: Security & Compliance

eSIM integration for MVNOs prioritizes strong security measures to protect user data. The solution provides data encryption for eSIM profiles, multi-factor authentication for user verification, and regular security audits and penetration tests. eSIMs maintain compliance with all global standards and regulations to establish customer trust while avoiding legal consequences.
Phase 5: Platforms like Spenza

End-to-end ESiM deployment support comes from platforms like Spenza . These platforms deliver API-based connectivity management, scalable reselling with global reach, integrated dashboards for real-time monitoring, and future-proof solutions for emerging technologies like 5G. The integration process becomes significantly more streamlined through this approach.
How MVNOs Leverage eSIM Technology

The eSIM technology, which experts say will transform the telecom sector, is what grabs attention, and micro operators, or MVNOs, stand ready to benefit from this technology. eSIMs will enhance MVNOs’ customer satisfaction through operational efficiency and create fresh business possibilities. Let’s take a closer look at how MVNOs can leverage eSIM integration:

Streamlined Operations & Reduced Costs: eSIM technology simplifies business operations and reduces expenses. Eliminating physical SIM cards removes costs associated with printing, packaging, transportation, and inventory management. These savings allow MVNOs to redirect funds to critical areas like marketing and customer service, while modernizing back-office operations. Enhanced Customer Experience: The integration of eSIMs offers faster activation times and easier device connections for users. Customers can activate services directly from their devices without waiting for physical SIM cards or visiting stores, improving satisfaction and convenience. Increased Flexibility & Choice for Customers: eSIM technology allows subscribers to switch mobile plans or providers without needing new physical SIM cards. MVNOs can differentiate themselves by offering customized plans, empowering customers to take full control over their mobile plans. Expanded Global Reach: eSIM technology supports international roaming by providing native network access abroad. Customers benefit from complete connectivity without incurring high roaming charges or experiencing dropped connections, enabling MVNOs to offer global connectivity without geographical restrictions. Simplified Device Management for IoT: eSIMs are especially beneficial for MVNOs in the IoT sector, offering efficient device management through remote provisioning and updates. This is vital for large-scale IoT deployments where physical access is limited, offering better scalability and streamlined operations.

eSIM has become a core technology for modern IoT connectivity, enabling MVNOs to deploy devices faster, reduce operational complexity, and deliver flexible multi-network services at scale. As enterprise IoT and 5G adoption continue to grow, MVNOs that invest in remote provisioning, centralized connectivity management, and scalable eSIM platforms will be better positioned to support global deployments and evolving customer requirements.

twoCol.text: Traditional SIM cards create roaming restrictions, logistical complexity, scalability bottlenecks, and security vulnerabilities. eSIM overcomes these issues through remote activation, native network access, simplified provisioning, and stronger protection against physical tampering.

twoCol.title: Successful eSIM Adoption Requires the Right Implementation Strategy
twoCol.text: MVNOs should begin with strategic planning, build a secure provisioning framework, integrate billing and CRM systems through APIs, and implement strong security and compliance measures. A scalable platform simplifies deployment and supports long-term growth.

twoCol.title: eSIM Creates New Business Opportunities for MVNOs
twoCol.text: By eliminating physical SIM logistics, eSIM reduces operating costs, accelerates customer activation, improves global connectivity, enhances customer experience, and simplifies IoT device management. These advantages enable MVNOs to expand services while improving operational efficiency.

oneCol.title: How Spenza Accelerates MVNO eSIM Success
oneCol.text: Spenza provides an end-to-end eSIM platform with secure provisioning, global connectivity APIs, scalable reselling capabilities, real-time monitoring, and coverage across 200+ countries. This enables MVNOs to launch faster, simplify operations, expand globally, and manage IoT connectivity through a unified platform.

blocks.text: Introduction

The industrial landscape is bustling with change, a real tech makeover. Think about it: oil rigs, sprawling warehouses, intricate logistics hubs, and bustling factories are all getting much “smarter.” Welcome to Industry 4.0, where smart systems, automation that just keeps going, and data that’s always live are completely changing how we work alongside machines. But here’s the thing – all this progress needs rock-solid, adaptable, and scalable communication to really work its methods.

Enter the IoT MVNO (Mobile Virtual Network Operator), a specialized partner that swoops in with connectivity solutions tailor-made for industrial automation. In this blog post, we’re going to dive into why IoT MVNOs are becoming increasingly vital in this space, and how platforms like Spenza are making it easier than ever for businesses to launch and grow their own MVNOs.
What Is Industry 4.0?

So, what exactly is Industry 4.0? It’s basically the fourth big wave of industrial revolution – an era defined by these super smart factories, interconnected cyber-physical systems, and machines that talk to each other. At its core, Industry 4.0 is all about bringing together:

The Internet of Things (IoT) – everyday objects getting connected. Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Machine Learning (ML) – making sense of all that data and enabling smart decisions. Robotics and automation – machines doing the heavy lifting and repetitive tasks. Cloud and edge computing – processing power wherever it’s needed. Digital twins and real-time analytics – virtual copies of physical assets giving us instant insights.

The big idea? Boost efficiency, cut down on downtime, and make operations super responsive to what the market wants. But guess what? None of this can happen without connectivity that you can really rely on and that can handle the workload – and that’s where IoT MVNOs step into the spotlight.
Why Connectivity Is Crucial for Industry 4.0

If Industry 4.0 is the powerful engine driving industrial automation forward, then connectivity is the fuel that keeps it roaring. As factories, warehouses, and all sorts of industrial sites get smarter, they become totally reliant on a massive network of connected machines – from simple sensors and cameras all the way to those autonomous robots and entire production lines. The catch? These environments are seriously complex, and they demand way more than just a basic Wi-Fi signal or your standard mobile data plan.
Let’s break it down a bit:

Real-Time Reactions Need Lightning-Fast Connections In a smart factory, timing is absolutely everything. Whether it’s a robotic arm precisely assembling parts or an AI-powered camera instantly spotting a defect, data needs to move now . Even a tiny delay in communication can throw things off, lead to faulty products, or even create safety hazards. That’s why super-low latency connectivity isn’t just a nice-to-have anymore – it’s a must-have.

Downtime? Not an Option. Industrial systems often run around the clock, and even a few minutes of being offline can mean lost productivity, missed deadlines, and some seriously hefty costs. Reliable, always-on connectivity is crucial to keep all those machines in sync, the systems running smoothly, and those vital supply chains moving without a hitch.

Growing Shouldn’t Be a Headache Modern manufacturers need to be able to scale up quickly – whether they’re launching a brand-new product line or expanding into a different part of the world. The connectivity infrastructure needs to keep pace. That means being able to add thousands of new connected devices without having to completely rethink your network or haggle with a bunch of different telecom providers.

Your Data Needs Fort Knox-Level Protection Machines aren’t just physical things doing work – they’re also constantly generating data. This data is often super sensitive, tied to things like product quality, production schedules, or even when machines might need maintenance. With cyberattacks becoming more and more common, keeping that data safe while it’s being transmitted is just as important as protecting the physical machines themselves.

One Network Just Doesn’t Cut It Let’s face it, no single mobile carrier has perfect coverage everywhere – especially in those tricky industrial locations like deep inside warehouses, down in mines, or across vast port areas. If you’re stuck with just one mobile network, you’re leaving yourself vulnerable to dead spots and unreliable connections. That’s why more and more businesses are looking at multi-carrier solutions that let their devices automatically connect to the strongest signal available, no matter where they are.

The bottom line? Traditional mobile providers weren’t really designed with these super smart factories in mind. They focus on what consumers need – phones, streaming videos, social media – not the unique, mission-critical demands of all these connected machines. And that’s precisely where IoT MVNOs really shine.
Enter the IoT MVNO: A New Kind of Connectivity Provider
Traditional mobile operators (MNOs) are great for consumer needs. But industrial IoT requires something more specialized—and that’s exactly where IoT MVNO s come in.

Think of an IoT MVNO as a connectivity partner built from the ground up for businesses running complex, distributed machine networks. They don’t own cell towers, but they lease infrastructure from multiple MNOs and wrap it in purpose-built services for IoT.
Here’s what makes them different—and better—for Industry 4.0:
Multi-Carrier Coverage Without the Contracts

Instead of being locked into one carrier, MVNOs give you access to multiple networks. That means your devices can always connect to the strongest, most reliable signal—whether they’re in a warehouse in California, a factory in Germany, or a logistics center in Singapore. It’s seamless, global, and ready to scale.
Data Plans Designed for Machines

A smartwatch might use a few megabytes a day. An HD video sensor on a production line could need several gigabytes an hour. MVNOs understand that every device is different—and they build connectivity plans to match. You’re not paying for unlimited data you’ll never use or trying to squeeze all your devices into a one-size-fits-all plan.
One Platform to Rule Them All

Managing thousands of devices across multiple carriers can be a nightmare—unless you have a unified management platform. IoT MVNOs offer centralized dashboards and APIs that make it easy to monitor SIM usage, set alerts, push updates, and more. No spreadsheets. No manual processes. Just clean, efficient control.
Built for eSIM, iSIM, and the Future

Gone are the days of swapping physical SIM cards. IoT MVNOs support remote provisioning through eSIM and iSIM , making it possible to onboard or update devices over the air—even if they’re embedded in machinery or deployed in hard-to-reach places. That’s a huge advantage in industrial environments where downtime or device access is limited.
Networks Designed for Machines, Not Humans

Your phone and your factory sensor don’t speak the same language. MVNOs optimize their networks for machine-to-machine communication , using lightweight protocols and architectures that are built for bursty data, low-power devices, and edge processing. This machine-first approach leads to faster performance and better battery life across your IoT ecosystem.
Industry-Grade Service and Support

Consumer-grade SLAs won’t cut it in manufacturing or logistics. MVNOs offer enterprise-grade support, guaranteed uptime, and integration services that are actually designed for operational technology (OT) teams. That means fewer outages, faster support, and better peace of mind.
How IoT MVNOs Support Industrial Automation
Let’s look at how IoT MVNOs contribute to automation in Industry 4.0 environments:

Reliable connectivity for autonomous systems: Whether it’s autonomous mobile robots (AMRs) in warehouses or robotic arms in assembly lines, consistent network performance is non-negotiable. IoT MVNOs provide multi-carrier fallback options to reduce downtime. Real-time analytics & monitoring: Factories and logistics operations rely on real-time data. IoT MVNOs offer low-latency, high-availability connections that enable this constant feedback loop. Remote management of endpoints: Using IoT MVNO portals, companies can push updates, monitor device health, and enforce policies remotely — essential for managing widely distributed assets. Scalable rollouts across regions: With a single interface to manage global SIM profiles, organizations can scale operations into new regions without renegotiating carrier deals or physically swapping SIMs. Secure transmission of operational data: From machine telemetry to video streams, data must be encrypted and compliant. MVNOs often offer features like private APNs and IPsec tunneling for enhanced security. Plug-and-play support: Zero-touch provisioning that ensures the device just works.
Benefits of Using MVNOs in Smart Manufacturing
The move to Industry 4.0 is fundamentally about speed, agility, and intelligence. Here’s why smart manufacturers are leaning into IoT MVNOs:

Faster time to market: MVNOs help new factories go live without waiting for fiber installs or long carrier negotiations. Lower operational costs: MVNOs offer IoT-specific plans, avoiding the bloated pricing of traditional unlimited plans. Better service control: Unlike MNOs, MVNOs offer customizable platforms to monitor, provision, and troubleshoot devices. Network independence: A factory in Mexico and one in Germany can use the same MVNO with local carriers in each region. Lower TCO (Total Cost of Ownership): As there are zero connectivity-related support issues that enterprises face with IoT MVNO-enabled devices, there is a lower cost of incident management and IT support.
Real-World Use Cases of MVNOs in Industry 4.0
Let’s take a look at where IoT MVNOs are already making a difference.

Automotive Manufacturing Plants: Robots and AGVs rely on real-time instructions and telemetry. Using an MVNO with low-latency cellular allows flexible deployment without costly rewiring. Smart Energy Grids: Smart meters and substation monitoring devices are often in remote areas. MVNOs enable continuous coverage by aggregating multiple carriers for redundancy. Food Processing Plants: IoT sensors monitor temperature, humidity, and spoilage risks. With an MVNO, these sensors send real-time alerts to centralized dashboards, ensuring compliance and quality. Angel Watch Case Study: Angel Watch, a company that manufactures child safety smartwatches, leveraged Spenza’s IoT MVNE platform to scale globally while keeping costs low. By offering region-specific, low-data plans and bundling services through their Shopify store, they created a seamless experience for parents — and a scalable business model for themselves.
Why Traditional Telcos Aren’t Enough
Legacy MNOs were built for consumers — voice, text, and high-data apps. They’re not optimized for:

Handling millions of low-data IoT devices. Creating flexible pricing models. Offering easy integration via APIs. Managing devices remotely through a self-serve portal. Supporting global scale without friction.
IoT MVNOs were built from the ground up with these requirements in mind.
How Spenza Enables IoT MVNOs to Scale in Industry 4.0

Spenza offers a Connectivity-as-a-Service platform purpose-built for launching and managing IoT MVNOs. Whether you’re a hardware company, logistics firm, or OEM looking to embed connectivity, Spenza provides:

Multi-carrier global access: Connect to 600+ networks across 190 countries. eSIM and SIM provisioning tools: Fully digital onboarding for new devices. Custom billing and bundling: Offer subscription models tailored to device usage. Real-time analytics and alerts: Keep operations optimized and cost-controlled. End-to-end lifecycle management: From provisioning to retirement.
Spenza empowers companies to launch branded connectivity offerings, optimize for cost, and drive new recurring revenue streams — all while simplifying connectivity in industrial environments.
Final Thoughts

Industry 4.0 is rewriting the rules of how products are built, moved, and maintained. At the center of this revolution is connectivity — and not just any kind. IoT MVNOs offer the flexibility, control, and scale needed to support complex industrial automation across global sites.

Companies like Angel Watch show what’s possible when connectivity isn’t just an afterthought — it’s a strategic asset. And with platforms like Spenza, launching an MVNO is more accessible than ever before.
